VCL PMO · Architecturepage 04 · 28 may 2026

Where each piece lives

We deliberately do not try to put everything in one tool. The principle is two anchors: ERPNext is the operational source of truth for project work, and Slack + Excel exist as downstream review surfaces that already work for the team.

Figure 3. One source of truth, two downstream review surfaces. No reverse writes from Slack or Excel back into ERPNext.

What that means in practice

  • You edit in ERPNext. Everything else mirrors automatically.
  • Slack is for reading and annotating. Plans land there as PDFs; nothing in Slack writes back.
  • Excel is for the monthly slice. n8n writes a workbook per project on the share; you never edit it directly.
  • Agents talk to ERPNext directly via whitelisted API methods. n8n is the routing layer, not a data store.

Visual reference

The PMO interface inside ERPNext follows a deliberate style language. These are the two mockups we built before settling on a direction. The live system follows the Mix A — Steel palette: light surface, navy frame, amber accents.

Mockup A — Steelmockups/mix-a.html
The Steel mockup: light surface, navy / amber accents, KPI tiles, requirement inbox. This is the styling reference for the report you're reading.
Mockup C — Pulsemockups/mix-c.html
The Pulse mockup: dark theme, live ticker, sparkline KPIs. Alternate visual treatment proposed but not built into /app/pmo yet.
